claims.text: Between approximately 600°C and 900°C, HfNbTaTiZr undergoes thermally activated localized atomic rearrangements or short-range-order fluctuations.
The localized atomic rearrangements reduce lattice strain or lattice distortion.
Relief of internal lattice distortion lowers barriers to dislocation motion.
Elevated temperature activates or increases dislocation mobility in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed atomic rearrangement causes the effective elastic modulus to decrease relative to its room-temperature value.
The proposed atomic rearrangement causes the thermal expansion coefficient to decrease relative to its room-temperature value.
The resulting high-temperature stress–strain curve will differ from the room-temperature curve.
The altered stress–strain response will include enhanced ductility or altered yielding behavior.
The initial as-cast or annealed HfNbTaTiZr microstructure is homogeneous.
At room temperature, HfNbTaTiZr has significant lattice distortion characteristic of multi-principal-element alloys.
At room temperature or below approximately 600°C, the alloy retains higher lattice distortion than it has in the proposed 600°C–900°C regime.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply under quasi-static loading between 600°C and 900°C.
Outside the stated temperature range, phase transformations or oxidation may control or alter the response.
Existing data are insufficient to establish the onset temperature and magnitude of the proposed rearrangement effects in HfNbTaTiZr.
